    public abstract class LRCMessageHandler
extends AbstractMessageHandler
    The parent class for all LRC message handlers. During the initialize(Map) method it will fetch a bunch of useful things from the properties and cache them in instance variables so that they can be accessed by child classes.

      • vetoUnlessForUsOrBroadcast

        protected void vetoUnlessForUsOrBroadcast(PorticoMessage request)
                                   throws VetoException
        This method will check the PorticoMessage to see if the kernel is an intended target of the message. To be a target, the request must have either NO stated target (so everyone is the target) or the target must have the same handle as the current federate. If the message is intended for someone else, a VetoException will be thrown.
        Throws:
        VetoException

      • vetoUnlessForUs

        protected void vetoUnlessForUs(PorticoMessage request)
                        throws VetoException
        This method will check the incoming request to see if the target federate handle is the same as the handle of the local federate (accessed through the LRCState). If the handles differ, a VetoException will be thrown, ending processing.
        Throws:
        VetoException

      • vetoIfMessageFromUs

        protected void vetoIfMessageFromUs(PorticoMessage request)
                            throws VetoException
        This method will check the source ID of the message and if it is the same as our federate handle, it will throw a VetoException, ending processing. This can be used by handlers if they want to filter out messages that they themselves generated (and thus might not need to process).
        Throws:
        VetoException

      • fill

        protected <T extends PorticoMessage> T fill(T instance)
        This will initialize the various parts of the given instance of the a PorticoMessage subclass and return it (so you can chain this call if you want). It will do things like set the source federate and timestamp based on the information from the LRCState. Note that the timestamp will only be added if the federate is regulating (as returned by LRCState.isRegulating().

      • moniker

        protected String moniker(int federateHandle)
        THis method returns a string that contains either the name or the handle of the identified federate. If logging with names is enabled for federates (see the documentation for PorticoConstants.isPrintHandlesForFederates()), the string will contain the federate name, otherwise it will contain the federate handle.

        NOTE: These methods are used to provide some consistency with the way various entities are logged. Using the xxmoniker() methods allows the user to define whether to use handle or names as a configuration option.

      • queueDummyAdvance

        protected void queueDummyAdvance()
        This method will queue up a dummy TimeAdvanceRequest that will force the LRC to reconsider whether any federates can issued time advance grants or not. Note that this dummy is never broadcast out over the network. It exists soley for inernal LRC use in situations like this.
